preparation: Avoid high-dose biotin supplements (>5 mg/day) at least 8 hours before the test

faqs.question: What does the Vitamin D Plus Profile Test include?
faqs.answer: It measures 25 OH Vitamin D and Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) to assess Vitamin D status and calcium-bone metabolism together.

faqs.question: Do I need to fast before the test?
Why is PTH tested along with Vitamin D?
faqs.answer: PTH reflects how the body is regulating calcium and phosphate. When interpreted with Vitamin D, it helps identify whether symptoms are due to deficiency, parathyroid dysfunction, or other metabolic causes.

faqs.question: What does low Vitamin D with high PTH mean?
faqs.answer: This commonly suggests Vitamin D deficiency with secondary hyperparathyroidism (a compensatory rise in PTH to maintain calcium balance).

faqs.question: Can supplements affect my test results?
faqs.answer: Yes. Vitamin D and calcium supplements can influence levels. Share details of recent supplementation with your clinician.

faqs.question: How often should I repeat this test?
faqs.answer: Your clinician may recommend retesting every 3–6 months, particularly when monitoring deficiency treatment or seasonal variation.

faqs.question: What happens if my Vitamin D levels are too high?
faqs.answer: Very high levels can suggest excessive supplementation and may be associated with high blood calcium. Your doctor will guide dose adjustment and any follow-up testing.
